title: The Flea and the Mouse

full_text:
In the opulent bedchamber of a wealthy chamberlain lived a little house mouse who had hollowed out a snug nest behind the cedar wainscoting. The mouse was prudent and modest, venturing out only in the dead of night to gather bread crumbs and melon seeds from the carpet, never chewing the fine tapestries or disturbing the master's sleep. Because of this discretion, the chamberlain never set traps or brought cats into the room.

One chilly evening, a wandering flea hopped through the window and begged for shelter: 'Brother mouse, the autumn frost is bitter outside. Grant me leave to warm myself by your nest for a single night, and I swear by the hospitality of the floorboards never to cause you grief.'

The kind mouse took pity on the shivering insect, fed him a drop of honey, and allowed him to rest. But as midnight struck, the aroma of the sleeping chamberlain’s warm bed proved too tempting for the flea’s greedy nature.

'Stay where you are!' warned the mouse. 'Our master sleeps soundly, but if you bite him, he will awaken in wrath, and both of us will perish.'

The arrogant flea scoffed at the warning: 'A tiny creature like me needs only one hearty sip. I shall be as light as a feather.' He hopped onto the bed, burrowed into the silk quilt, and bit the chamberlain so sharply on the neck that the nobleman leaped up shouting with pain!

The chamberlain summoned his servants with torches and brooms, commanding them to search every inch of the bedding, the curtains, and the wainscoting. The nimble flea leaped into a crack in the wall and escaped into the garden, but the poor, innocent mouse was discovered in his nest behind the baseboard.

The servants overturned the nest, driving the mouse into exile in the cold night. As the mouse shivered beneath a dry leaf, he lamented: 'Woe to him who welcomes an undisciplined guest! He who cannot control his own appetite brings ruin upon the roof that sheltered him.'
moral: Greed and impatience in a guest bring disaster upon both himself and his generous host.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Flea and the Mouse"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
